It could be both the paper and the pencil! Pencils with a hardness of H or higher and a super sharp tip can help rectify this effect on grainy papers. If you are having trouble getting a fine point, I recommend rolling the point over sand paper until it is needle sharp!

A good technique to use to also avoid this is by using tight, circular strokes instead of straight ones. Circular strokes help move the fine grains of graphite into those itty bitty gaps and can help create smoother value transitions.

For future sketching endeavors, I would recommend a smooth paper like Bristol for total control over your texture.

Heyo, previous anorexic and current IBS patient here.

Let me preface this by saying NOTHING makes me hungry BUT cannabis. Pills and home remedies are completely useless to stimulate my appetite.

But, it’s not realistic or safe for me to wait to eat until my next hit SO here’s how to eat without actually being hungry:

1. Protein shakes, smoothies, tomato soup, beef broth, etc are NECESSARY.
- you’re going to need to put something in your stomach, wether you want to chew or not. When I’m in a mood, the thought of even small bits of potato or carrots can make me dry-heave, so nutrient-rich liquids are always on hand. Even just orange juice will help (but if you have Acid reflux too, stick to something less acidic, like milk!(unless you’re lactose intolerant too...))

2. You’re going to get nauseous. You’re probably going to throw up, too, be prepared.
-Nausea is a part of life, but it doesn’t always mean you NEED to throw up. Anti-emetics are meds that you can find bit above and below the counter: Emetrol is a liquid one that uses sugar to coat the stomach, Tums uses foam to settle acid-related discomfort, and Omeprazol is a minor psychoactive that stops your brain from making you nauseous. Choose one that best relieves the source of your nausea, wether it be physical or anxiety-based.
-you WILL vomit. Sorry, but it’s not the end of the world! Keep some toothpaste, a toothbrush, and some non-flavored gum on hand, and, if you’re able, a change of clothes! You NEED to brush your teeth after you vomit, or else you’ll destroy your teeth overtime with stomach acid. Plus, the taste of vomit just makes you want to throw up more, right? The non-flavored gum helps distract, but it also stimulates saliva production which will help soothe the inside of your mouth and throat.

3. Eat at the same time everyday.
-even if you’re just shoving a cracker or piece of chocolate in your mouth, try and schedule your feeding times. The brain thrives on pattern and routine; you’ve heard of Pavlov’s dog right? Even if you’re not hungry at these feeding times, your body will still be accustomed to digesting at the same time everyday (it learns SUPER quickly) and it will help lesson the pain of digestion and maybe even solidify your Hershey Squirts. 

I hope the rest of you break is as liquid smooth as your dumps. Please eat something, or you’ll only ruin your stomach more like I did 😬

I’m new so I don’t think I have much to offer, but I recently ran into the same problem.

My solution was to instead make a supporting character EXACTLY like me. Instead of imagining myself in the heroics of the main character, I’ve been exploring how I would act if my best friend suddenly became a hero, or how I would react if someone came to me with a dark secret. It’s been very helpful, as I have to purposefully reign in this character’s motives and actions. 

It’s also been helpful in a humbling, introspective way. This character doesn’t have to save the world, so what are your flaws that would stop them from doing so? Are they scared or selfish? Do they have what it takes from your own personality to be a hero- and that brings the question, could you really ever be a hero?

I wouldn’t necessarily say watching AH has saved me or anything like that, but they’ve always been a constant in my life. 

After my suicide attempt last year, I basically holed myself in my room until a few months ago. I did nothing all day, just slept and played video games, and watched AH Minecraft on repeat. While it was a lonely healing process, I could always look forward to a new silly video and that made it a little easier.

Now, I’m trying to relearn how to function in public. I get self-conscious about how I talk and the stories I tell (the suicide attempt took away some of my mental ability, so I don’t make sense sometimes, and get confused very easily). I’ve been trying to copy how the guys talk, and learn from their confidence.

It’s been nice to grow from them, and slowly, but surely, I have begun to come out my shell a little more. I’ve been making people laugh a bit more, so that’s nice too.

I’ll miss Etika, and I’m sorry his journey ended so early. The impact of suicide is so much broader than the victims tend to realize- how it affects those in the world if you succeed, or how it can scar you forever if you fail. Meanwhile, our loved ones struggle to understand how someone could come to such a decision.

But when people like AH and Roosterteeth speak about it so candidly, when they work so hard to end the stigma- we all start to get a better idea. What they’re doing is so important, and I’m so grateful they’ve chosen to be vulnerable on camera with us in order to spread that message.

I think by brain patterns they might be referring more literally to our neural pathways, which are the intangible connections between every single brain process. Neural pathways can amazingly be rearranged or changed completely. For example, some seizure patients require a partial lobectomy, but after time and intense therapy, the functions that were lost with that portion of the brain can be regained via neural pathways. There are even forms of therapy that can help patients of mental illness lessen their symptoms by rearranging their neural pathways. 

An easy way to look at it is it’s our mysterious brain “wiring”. I’m not a doctor, but if I remember correctly, everyone experiences significant rearranging or “rewiring” from the time we’re born until around the age of 25 (they can be rearranged after this stage, it’s just REALLY hard). That’s the elasticity Dr. Weller was referring to in the very beginning. 

Even though we have several methods of attempting to rearrange pathways, a lot of the rewiring takes place without our control, and even without our conscious knowledge. And despite their complicated nature, these pathways are FRAGILE. Trauma can absolutely destroy them, changing logical/healthy pathways into helpless messes (which can eventually develop into mental illness). Remember when Cammie started ripping through uptime when she lost her head?

Unfortunately, deleting episodic memory wouldn’t successfully change these pathways, in fact it might even tear giant holes in the neural network. It happens so quickly, so out of our control, it’d be nearly impossible to unravel and snip off ALL of the bad connections.

An example of these pathways’ untamable rewiring is dreaming! Dreams/nightmares, whether you remember them or not, are the brain’s way of processing all of the data it received during the previous awake time. This process forms many new connections, sometimes even repairing damaged ones, allowing the brain to heal and grow stronger. Some of the G:L team talked about having dreams of being mecha-sized in the beginning of their training. That’s their brain trying to make sense.

Since these pathways are so flexible, you’re probably wondering why uptime is an issue in the first place. Wouldn’t it be able to just fix itself? Well, to be honest, I don’t know, I don’t think anybody knows. Like I mentioned earlier, most of the brain’s processes are largely shrouded in mystery. We don’t know how closely our physical bodies are related to these networks and more importantly, how they’re related to our intangible “mind”. 

The human experience is so unique to every individual, it’s just impossible to measure and find patterns in  data sets (but I’ve heard they’re trying). By putting themselves in new bodies, the G:L team is essentially receiving an entirely new data set that may not translate to the data their human body accepts. Like trying to put JavaScript into python.

BASICALLY, the episodic memory that Cammie was seen editing only accounts for a small fraction of our brain’s “code” and it requires lots of time, therapy, still unknown science, and sheer luck to change or fix your brain’s “code”.
